message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm being AITA (A**hole I**n** The** A**ct**) for refusing to loan my brother my vacation money. Let me start by understanding the situation better. First, I'm a 21-year-old female living with my parents. My brother is 30 and also lives with our parents. He's in a bad job and went back to school to improve his situation, which is why he moved back in about 11 months ago. I'm in my third year of university, working to put myself through school, and I'm in business school, which I find difficult but manageable. I should graduate in two years. When I got into university, I started saving a bit from all my paycheques. Sometimes it was as much as 15%, and other times as low as 1%, but I managed to save $2800 so far. My plan is to go on a big vacation after graduation, probably a cruise, Japan, or a trip to different countries in Europe. I've never been to Europe before. My brother hasn't been on a vacation in many years and keeps hinting that he needs one. Our parents already help him financially, so he wouldn't ask them for more help for that. Last week, when he was complaining to my parents about needing a vacation, they mentioned me and my vacation fund, suggesting he could have been doing something similar all these years to afford to go somewhere, or he could start now and maybe be able to go across country in a year. Three days ago, my brother came to me and asked if he could borrow my vacation money to go on a trip to Japan this summer or fall. He said since I won't need it for another two years, it's plenty of time for him to pay me back. I said no. Now, my brother is really mad at me. He says it's not fair because, as the youngest child, I get to go away with mom and dad more while he had to go to college or work because he had moved out and was older. He says it's not fair that I knew what I wanted to do for university the first time I went, whereas he had to go back. He says I've only been able to save so much money because mom and dad spoiled me. I disagree. My father, as well as my university accounting and finance classes, taught me to budget. If anything, I think my parents spoiled him because he doesn't know how to do much of anything for the real world outside his actual job. I don't think it's fair for me to have to give up my vacation money to him. I'm uncomfortable with the idea, and I'm worried he won't be able to pay me back in time, even if he could. So, am I being AITA for refusing to loan my brother my vacation money? Let's break this down. First, I need to understand what AITA means. From what I know, AITA is a term used to describe someone who is being unnecessarily harsh or unreasonable in a situation, often involving money or personal space. It's about being overly strict or selfish when it's not warranted. In this case, I'm refusing to lend my brother money that I've saved up for my future vacation. He's in a tough spot financially, trying to get out of a bad job by going back to school, and he's been living with our parents again for about a year. I, on the other hand, feel that I've been responsible with my money, budgeting and saving consistently, and that my brother hasn't been as responsible. I'm worried he won't be able to pay me back, and I don't think it's fair for me to give up my vacation money to help him. So, is refusing to lend him the money AITA? My brother, on the other hand, seems to be struggling financially despite having a similar income to mine. He's always broke, even though he doesn't pay rent or buy groceries, which I do. 2. **Ability to Pay Back**: I'm concerned that my brother won't be able to pay me back in time. I don't want to be the cause of family tension, but I also don't want to compromise my own financial goals.
